findings.claim: The new location filter still reports diagnostics for metadata members when the diagnostic location is null. Both changed call sites can now produce Location.None (GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null, and MemberNeedsKey uses FirstOrDefault()?.), but ReportIfLocatedInCompilation treats !Location.IsInSource as reportable. Consequently a consuming project can newly receive project-level MsgPack004/MsgPack005 diagnostics for a closed generic struct defined in a referenced assembly, despite metadata types being owned and diagnosed by their defining assembly; MsgPack004 is an error, so this can break the consuming build.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test with a metadata lib containing [MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T> with a public property lacking [Key] (and a second case with null int/string keys for MsgPack005), compiled without these diagnostics enforced there, and an app source [MessagePackObject] containing an Item<int> member. Run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on app and assert no AD0001 and no MsgPack004/MsgPack005 diagnostic is reported in app. The current code reports a Location.None diagnostic because the null-location branch calls report.
